newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Rival "camps" to be set up near Cyprus talks center.
newsitem.headline: Rival "camps" to be set up near Cyprus talks center.

text.p: Greek and Turkish Cypriots will set up separate headquarters near a rural retreat north of New York City next week when talks get under way on a long-stymied peace process to reunite the island.

Cypriot President Glafcos Clerides, representing the Greek Cypriots, and Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash are scheduled to meet from July 9 to 13 at Troutbeck 90 miles (145 kms) north of New York city.
While they and two advisers each will stay at the rural conference centre, members of their teams and other aides are staking out unofficial headquarters at hotels in the vicinity.
By living in rival "camps," the leaders will transplant to the countryside some characteristics of the partitioned island, which has been divided for more than two decades.

A third "camp" will comprise representatives of countries that have appointed special envoys to keep track of developments affecting Cyprus. The aim of the talks is to achieve a bi-zonal, bi-communal federation.

If all goes reasonably well, another couple of rounds of talks are anticipated before a break during a presidential election campaign in the Greek Cypriot-controlled south of the island leading up to a vote next February.

Mirroring the division of Cyprus itself, the Greek Cypriot "headquarters" will be a hotel at Poughkeepsie, New York, a few miles southwest of Troutbeck. A rival Turkish Cypriot "camp" is to be set up at a hotel in Salisbury, Connecticut, a few miles northeast of Troutbeck.

Some of the special representatives of interested governments are planning to put up at a motel at Millbrook, New York, which lies between the Greek Cypriot hotel at Poughkeepsie and the conference site.

When Clerides and Denktash first arrive on Sunday or Monday they will stay at different hotels in Manhattan. The two leaders, accompanied by one adviser each, will also attend a dinner that Secretary-General Kofi Annan is to give at his Manhattan residence on Tuesday night.

A long list of other invitees is expected to include Annan's special adviser for Cyprus, former Ecuadorean Foreign Minister Diego Cordovez; the under-secretaries-general for political affairs and for peacekeeping, and the senior resident U.N. official in Cyprus, Gustave Feissel.

Also invited will be the special representatives of countries that are closely following the Cyprus issue as well as envoys from the European Union. Turkey occupied northern Cyprus in 1974 in an invasion sparked by a brief Greek Cypriot coup engineered by the military then ruling Greece.
